chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Fasting on the day of Eid-e Ghadeer is the expiation for sixty years.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting on the day of Eid al-Ghadir according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the unique status of Eid al-Ghadir as a day of divine celebration, equating the reward of fasting on this day to the expiation of sixty years of sins. This immense merit reflects the theological weight of the Declaration of Ghadir, marking the completion of the message and the establishment of Imamate, thereby transforming a simple act of worship into a commemoration of divine perfection. The comparison to sixty years highlights the rarity and magnitude of this specific occasion within the Shia liturgical calendar.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. It was narrated to us by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said it was narrated to us by Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim who said it was narrated to us by Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Muffadhal b. Umar from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
Fasting on the day of Eid-e- Ghadeer is equal to the compensation of sins committed in sixty years.”
